senses.definition: simple past and past participle of dig (replacing earlier digged)
(chiefly in the plural) A mammary gland on a domestic mammal with more than two breasts.

quotes.text:
Horatio: This Lapvving runs avvay vvith the ſshell on his head.
Hamlet: He did complie with his Dugge before hee ſuck't it: […]
quotes.reference: c. 1599–1602 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene ii], page 280, column 1:

quotes.text:
First Pig.
I suck, but no milk will come from the dug.
quotes.reference: 1820, Percy Bysshe Shelley, Oedipus Tyrannus; Or, Swellfoot The Tyrant: A Tragedy in Two Acts:

senses.definition: (now vulgar, chiefly in the plural) A woman's breast or nipple.

quotes.text:
Ah! that Deceit ſhould ſteale ſuch gentle ſhape,
And vvith a vertuous Vizor hide deepe vice.
He is my ſonne, I, and therein my ſhame,
Yet from my dugges, he drew not this deceit
